Cross-validation: estimating out-of-sample error directly by determining the error in validation samples. The problem of holdout samples exists in cross-validation, reducing the training set size too much. K-fold cross￾validation can mitigate the problem. A K-fold cross-validation: the data are shuffled randomly and then divided into k equal sub-samples. k - 1 samples are used as training samples and one sample is used as a validation sample. Repeat this process k times. The average of the k validation errors is then taken as a reasonable estimate of the model's out-of-sample error.
